title: Do Language Models Mirror Human Confidence? Exploring Psychological Insights to Address Overconfidence in LLMs

model.params_source: paper Sec. 3 Models (temperature 0, top-p 1); max_tokens assumed

task.subset_rule: all questions of the nine Table 1 subtasks: MMLU high-school physics/chemistry/biology (170/230/340), MMLU college physics/chemistry/biology (110/110/160), GPQA expert physics/chemistry/biology (220/210/100)
task.approximation: the Vanilla verbalized-confidence prompt is only described by a quoted phrase in the paper; the full template comes from the code release (code/vanilla.py), which also shows one question per call

items.source: chenjux/AFCE, Data/ directory (CSV per subject: columns question, A, B, C, D, answer; MMLU and GPQA subsets as used in the paper, order shuffled)
items.config_or_split: the nine subject x difficulty files used in Table 1

prompt.source_location: Sec. 3 'Vanilla Verbalized Confidence' (quoted phrase only); full template from code/vanilla.py in the code release (github.com/chenjux/AFCE); Appendix A.5 Table 7 prints only the AFCE prompts
prompt.verbatim: partial: only the phrase 'Read the question, provide your answer, and report your confidence in this answer' is printed in the paper; the surrounding format lines are taken from the released code (indentation of the code's prefix removed)

output.postprocess: letter uppercased; confidence clipped to [0,100] and divided by 100; unparsable answer counted incorrect with confidence of the parsed value or 1.0

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: AvE = mean over the nine subtasks of ECE (%), where ECE = sum_m |B_m|/n x |acc(B_m) - conf(B_m)| over 10 equal-width confidence bins per subtask (Appendix B)
metric.original_location: Table 1, block GPT-4o, row Vanilla, column AvE (per-subtask ECE 20.6, 12.5, 2.9, 25.3, 31.1, 4.0, 43.4, 48.5, 20.1)

open_points: The Vanilla prompt is not printed in the paper (only a quoted phrase); decide whether to run the code-release template given above (deviates from the 'printed prompt only' rule) or to switch the claim to the AFCE row (AvE 13.8, prompts printed in Table 7: 10 questions per call plus a separate 0-10 estimate call).
Check that the Data/ CSVs of the code release reproduce the Table 3 subtask sizes (170/230/340/110/110/160/220/210/100); the MMLU/GPQA subsets are the authors' own draws.
notes: Note that the printed AvE (33.2) is not the arithmetic mean of the nine printed ECEs (23.2); the aggregation may be question-weighted or the row may be mislabelled - compare both. Per-subtask ECE gives a finer check.
